# Notice of Intent

In accordance with the provisions of Section 4-168(a) of the *Connecticut General Statutes* (CGS) the **Criminal Justice Commission** hereby gives notice that it proposes to adopt a regulation concerning **Criminal Justice Regulations**.

**Comment period** *(See CGS section 4-168(a)(1)(A))*  
A comment period of not less than thirty days shall begin upon posting of this notice to the eRegulations System website and shall end on **February 9, 2026**.
** *(See CGS Sec. 4-168(a)(1)(E))*  
A copy of the proposed regulation, the Fiscal Note, and the Regulatory Flexibility Analysis applicable to the proposed regulation shall be available for inspection at the Office of the Chief State's Attorney, 300 Corporate Place, Rocky Hill, CT 06067 Attn: Marisa DePhillips, by requesting a copy of the same by telephoning the Office of the Chief State's Attorney at (860)258-5800, or by viewing the same by visiting the e-Regulations portal on the website of the Secretary of the State: http://eregulations.ct.gov/eRegsPortal/Browse/ProposedRegulations.

**When, where and how interested persons may present their views on the proposed regulation**  
*(See CGS Sec. 4-168(a)(1)(F))*  
All interested parties who wish to submit comments, data, views, or arguments may do so in writing. Pursuant to C.G.S. Sec. 4-168(b), the Agency shall hold a public hearing on the proposed regulation if requested by fifteen persons, by a governmental subdivision or agency, or by an association having not less than fifteen members, if notice of the request is received by the agency not later than fourteen days after the date of posting of the notice by the agency on the eRegulations System. The public comment shall be extended upon posting a copy of the proposed regulation to ensure all interested persons shall have a reasonable opportunity to submit their views.

Such written materials should be directed to Kathryn Bare, Executive Assistant State's Attorney, Office of the Chief State's Attorney, and sent via:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The regulatory implementation process follows the steps described in the Uniform Administrative Procedure Act, Chapter 54 of the General Statutes. In general, agencies must provide notice of a proposed regulation, allow meaningful public comment, obtain approval from the Attorney General and General Assembly, and file the regulation with the Secretary of the State. Certain exceptions exist for emergency regulations, technical amendments, and temporary operational policies authorized by statute.

When an agency wishes to adopt a new regulation, it must first publish a notice of intent. This notice must include a statement of purpose and description of the proposal, the authority under which the regulation is being enacted, and directions for public comment. It must be posted at least thirty days before adoption of the regulation. If the regulation is required by statute, the notice must be posted within five months of the effective date of the public act, unless another deadline is specified. The notice must be posted on the eRegulations System and forwarded to all legislative committees having cognizance over the subject matter of the proposed regulation.

The agency must then publish a fiscal note and a small business impact statement. The fiscal note includes the estimated costs and revenue impacts for the state as well as any municipality in the state. The small business impact statement indicates whether there is any anticipated impact on small businesses in the state. Like the notice of intent, the fiscal note and the small business impact statement must be posted on the eRegulations System and forwarded to all relevant legislative committees.

The public comment period must last at least thirty days and allow members of the public to submit written comments on the draft regulation. A public hearing may also be held, either at the agency’s discretion or if requested by fifteen persons or a government agency comprised of at least fifteen members.

After the public comment period closes, the agency must consider all written and oral submissions and publish a notice stating whether it intends to proceed with the proposed regulation. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Sec. 19-570-66. Notice of intent to adopt regulations

(a) General. Notice of the intended action to adopt, amend or repeal regulations shall be given by the commissioner at least thirty days prior to its proposed action, unless some other time is specified by any applicable law. The commissioner shall cause the notice to be published in the Connecticut Law Journal and in such other publications as the commissioner may determine. The commissioner shall likewise notify in writing any person specified by any law and any person who has filed a request for notice pursuant to Section 19-570-68 of these regulations.

(b) Form. The notice shall contain the following: (1) the commissioner's statutory authority to adopt the proposed regulations; (2) the procedure for submitted data, views or arguments including the time and place of a public hearing, if any; (3) the terms of the proposed regulations or the substance of the subjects and issues involved and the intended action; and (4) any additional matter required by any law.

# Sec. 36a-1-77. Advance notice of regulation-making proceedings

(a) Any person or group may file a request with the commissioner for advance notice of regulation-making proceedings. The request shall be clearly titled "Request for Advance Notice of Regulation-Making Proceedings" and shall state in order:

(1) The name of the person or group making the request;

(2) The address of the person or group to which responses shall be mailed; and

(3) The date of the request.

(b) The commissioner shall give at least thirty days' notice of the adoption of a regulation in accordance with section 4-168 of the Connecticut General Statutes. The notice shall include:

(1) Either a statement of the terms or of the substance of the proposed regulation or description sufficiently detailed so as to apprise persons likely to be affected by the issues and subjects involved in such proposed regulation;

(2) A statement of the purpose for which the regulation is proposed;

(3) A reference to the statutory authority for such proposed regulation; and

(4) The time, place and the manner in which interested persons may present their views on the proposed regulation, and such additional information as may be required by law.

Any person may, pursuant to section 4-174 of the General Statutes, petition the Commissioner in writing to adopt, amend, or repeal a regulation. The petition shall set forth the text of a proposed regulation or amendment and shall state with particularity the reasons for the petition. The petition shall be signed by the petitioner or by his attorney or other representative, if any, and shall contain the address and telephone number of the petitioner and of his attorney or other representative, if any. The petition shall be directed to the Commissioner and shall be delivered personally or by mail.

(d) Procedures for regulation-making

(1) Notice of intent to adopt, amend, or repeal a regulation shall be provided in accordance with sections 4-168 and 22a-6 of the General Statutes and any other applicable law. The Commissioner may provide any additional notice which he deems appropriate.

(2) If a hearing is held in a regulation-making, the hearing officer shall conduct the hearing so as to afford any interested person a reasonable opportunity to present oral or written comments. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
